Sam (AE): MerchantCo asked for a compact runbook: how we plan to meet 99th <= 400ms during their 45-min morning spike. They want reserved GPUs + optional burst credits. Questionnaire deadline Thu noon.
Priya (SE): Quick clarifying Qs: peak qps, avg tokens per turn, acceptable degrade (ie p99 500ms acceptable?), and do they accept model fallbacks?
Sam (AE): Peak = 900 qps, avg in+out = 250 tokens, strict p99 target 400ms (no degrade), fallback to smaller model only as a last resort.
Jordan (SRE): Ok. Real-world plan: reserve baseline GPUs to cover steady-state + preheat KV cache before spike. Use autoscale with buffer and a small burst-credit pool. Fallbacks only after operator approval.
Theo (Infra): My quick calc for redwood-13b-quant: single GPU sustained throughput ~120 qps @avg_seq=250 with batching. So baseline GPUs = ceil(100 qps /120) = 1 for steady 100 qps, but for headroom and cold-start we recommend min=5 reserved. For 900 qps peak, need ~8 GPUs (900/120=7.5). Add burst pool +2.
Mira (Sales Ops): They want a cost comparison: reserved-only vs reserved + burst credits. Can someone toss simple numbers? Use token-cost proxy: $0.0003 per 1k tokens for reserved mgmt, burst marginal 25% premium.
Priya (SE): Worked example (round numbers): peak 250 tokens/request * 900 qps = 225k tokens/s -> 13.5M tokens/min. Using $0.0003/1k tokens -> cost = 13.5M/1k * 0.0003 = $4,050/min. If 60% served from KV cache (reduced model work), effective token billing drops ~60% -> $1,620/min. Burst premium 25% -> $2,025/min. We'll include monthly example for a 30-day month and a 2-hour/day spike.
Jordan (SRE): Important: KV cache hit-rate assumption matters. For chat with high prefix reuse we can hit 50-70% easily with a good preheat. We'll commit to a 30-minute preheat job before the window and synthetic traffic to seed top N prefixes.
Sam (AE): Customer insisted on proof during POC  can we schedule a live demo showing p99 under 400ms?
Jordan (SRE): Yes. Plan: smoke test in staging that mirrors production qps shape (ramp to 900 qps over 5 min). We'll record p50/p95/p99, and provide log slices. ops-bot will annotate run.
ops-bot: Staging smoke test scheduled: 2024-07-02T14:00:00Z. Artifacts will be uploaded to /artifacts/merchantco/poc-smoke-20240702.
Legal (Contracts): On KMS: merchant wants statement in questionnaire about key custody and rotation. Suggested clause: "Customer-managed KMS is supported; customers may rotate keys on their schedule. Redwood can perform managed rotation on behalf of the customer under a documented process; default managed rotation cadence is 90 days."
Mira (Sales Ops): I'll include that. Also need wording for audit log export and retention.
Theo (Infra): Export note: we can stream AuditEvents to customer S3 or Pub/Sub. Retention: default 90 days on Redwood; enterprise retention add-on available.
Priya (SE): Autoscale policy I recommend to include in runbook:
```
policy_name: merchantco-linear
min_gpus: 5
max_gpus: 12
scale_step: 1
cooldown_sec: 45
warmup_window: 900  # 15 minutes
burst_pool: 2
kv_preheat: true
```
This gives controlled ramp and room for burst credits.
Sam (AE): Action items: Priya runs a refined perf sim and posts numbers by Tue EOD. Theo provisions staging reservation and burst pool. Jordan schedules smoke test and prepares run artifacts. Mira drafts pricing scenarios and questionnaire answers. Legal to sign off KMS wording.
Mira (Sales Ops): I'll draft two pricing scenarios: (A) 5 GPU reserved baseline + token billing during spike; (B) 8 GPU reserved baseline with lower token-overage. Will share spreadsheet link.
Priya (SE): One more note: if customer chooses Private deployment, throughput per-GPU may differ slightly due to network and on-prem constraints; call that out in POC assumptions.
Sam (AE): Timeline: questionnaire Thu noon, perf sim Tue EOD, staging prep Wed, smoke Fri. Are we aligned?
Jordan (SRE): Aligned. I'll add a short runbook for on-call during live demo.
Theo (Infra): Provisioning started in staging. Sharing ARNs and network CIDR in the deal doc.
Sam (AE): Thanks team, I'll reply to MerchantCo with the plan and tentative pricing examples. :thumbsup:
